Q: How to apply a function to every column in a dataframe A:

Seems like the operation should be applied to all columns. Looping over columns is often acceptable, you can adapt to

for (i in seq_along(X)) X[[i]] = X[[i]] / sd(X[[i]])

For the fun

sweep(X, 2L, Rfast::rowVars(t(X), std=TRUE), '/')

Q: Fastest way(s) to move the cursor on a terminal command line? A:

You have two options to be fast:
1. bash(emacs) shortcuts
2. set to vim mode

Vim Mode (the fastest)

vi mode would be the fastest if you know vim:

set -o vi

you can make this permenant by setting at .bashrc or .zshrc

Bash Mode

for bash shortcuts there are too many of them. But I've extracted the most useful ones and categorised them as follows:

Moving

ctrl + a Go to beginning to command line ctrl + e Go to End of command line ctrl + b Move back one character ctrl + f Move forward one character alt + b Move cursor back one WORD alt + f Move cursor forward one WORD ctrl + xx Toggle between the start of line and current cursor position

Edit / Other

(i'll add these later)

History

ctrl + p Fetch the previous command from the history list, moving back in the list (same as Up arrow) ctrl + n Fetch the next command from the history list, moving forward in the list (same as Down arrow) ctrl + o Execture the command found via Ctrl + r or Ctrl + s ctrl + r Search backward starting at the current line and moving UP through the history as necessary ctrl + s Search forward starting at the current line and moving DOWN through the history as necessary ctrl + g Escape from history searching mode

less common

!! Run Previous command !$ last argument of last command !^ First argumeent of last command !n Execute nth command in history ^abc^xyz Replace first occurance of abc with xyz in last command and execute it
